transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Well, what actually made me call the EAP to set this up is... I've been having this issue at work lately. Every little bang in the office, like a file drawer shutting or someone dropping a coffee mug, it makes me jump really hard. And it's not just that I jump, my chest starts racing and it just keeps going way longer than it should. It's getting pretty distracting, so I figured I needed to come talk to someone about it.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a particularly traumatic or life-threatening event?

Life-threatening? No, not that I can think of. I mean, I haven't been in a bad car accident or anything like that. I'm not really sure what else you mean by traumatic, but nothing major comes to mind. That's part of why this is so weird for me, to be honest.
Aside from these physical reactions to noises, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of everyday matters?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like hitting my sales targets for the quarter or making sure my team is staying on track, but it's not like I'm constantly stressed about every little thing. It's just these sudden noises that really set me off.
Do these intense physical sensations, like your heart racing, ever happen completely out of the blue without any loud noise or trigger?

No, not really. It's pretty much always tied to a noise. If it's quiet, I'm fine. I don't just sit there and suddenly feel my heart going crazy for no reason. It's always right after a loud bang or something dropping.
Do you find yourself dreading or trying to avoid situations or places where you think loud noises might happen?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't go out of my way to avoid places. I still go to work, go to the store, things like that. I guess I'm a little more on edge if I know I'm going somewhere noisy, like a construction site near the office or something, but I wouldn't say I dread it or try to get out of it. I just deal with it when it happens.
How long have you been experiencing these reactions to sudden noises?
It's been going on for about two weeks now. It all started right after this really intense, late-night confrontation I had with my regional boss.
During that confrontation with your boss, was there any physical violence or threat of physical harm?

No, there wasn't anything like that. It was just a lot of yelling, really loud and aggressive, but he didn't hit me or threaten to hurt me physically or anything. It was just... a really heated, awful argument.
Has this reaction been interfering with your ability to do your job or manage your daily responsibilities?

Well, I'm still making it to work every day, so I'm getting there. But... it is definitely affecting me. I'm just slower with everything right now, especially going over the accounts and making staffing decisions. I've actually had to ask my team to double-check a few things that I would normally just handle on my own without a second thought. It's frustrating. And honestly, with performance reviews coming up soon, I'm pretty worried that these little mistakes or delays are going to end up affecting my job.
